At a least-weight coordinate the sign-gradient witness has Lipschitz norm one on every edge and attains that directional constant. Transitivity gives equal directional constants, proving both the universal sharp norm and arbitrary weight-independence. Binomial sign counting proves the homogeneous-layer specialization. value.rationale: The theorem determines a natural Banach-space relative projection constant for every coordinate-transitive spectral family on every finite weighted Boolean cube, simultaneously in dimension, spectrum and continuously varying positive weights. Arbitrarily severe anisotropy changes the ambient norm and destroys coordinate-permutation metric symmetry, yet the optimum stays exactly fixed. A constructive extremizer and exact Krawtchouk layer formulas give an effective classification; this phenomenon does not hold for all asymmetric spectral families and is not merely an isolated small-dimensional computation.
